poem_stanzas:
I rise from the deep and roll toward the shore
A moving hill of water that never stands still
The moon pulls me and the wind decides my height
I curl, I break, I crash, and then I am gone

Surfers wait for me and sailors dread my size
I travel across the ocean for a thousand miles
A stadium crowd performs me with their hands
And I can also mean a greeting or a curl of hair
ciphers.hint: A rolling ridge of water crossing the sea.

poem_stanzas:
I am born in a thundercloud's cold heart
A frozen pebble that falls in summer's heat
I drum on roofs and bruise the tender garden
Then vanish into puddles where I land

Round as a marble, hard as a bead of ice
I fall in armies when the sky is angry
Farmers dread my brief and battering visit
And children gather me before I melt
ciphers.hint: A pellet of ice flung from a storm.

poem_stanzas:
A shallow mirror left by yesterday's rain
I hold a broken piece of sky in my palm
Children stamp me and I scatter into rings
Then settle back to glass without a ripple

I live in the hollow of a worn-out road
I vanish when the sun remembers to shine
Ducks and sparrows drink from my brief ocean
And boots baptize me on a school-day morning
ciphers.hint: A small pool left behind by a shower.

poem_stanzas:
Still and green, I keep the lilies on my back
A frog's whole kingdom ringed by reeds and stone
I do not hurry anywhere, I simply stay
And hold the clouds as if they were my own

Ducks paddle across my face without a wake
The moon sleeps on me like a fallen coin
I am smaller than a lake, deeper than a bath
And patient as the willow at my edge
ciphers.hint: A quiet sheet of water in a garden.

poem_stanzas:
Ground that swallows footsteps with a sucking kiss
A sponge of rotting moss where no path is firm
I smell of ancient water, peat, and time
And keep old bones beneath my shaggy green

Fire sleeps inside my layers, dark and slow
Men cut me into bricks to warm their homes
I am neither land nor lake but something between
Treacherous and soft beneath the heather
ciphers.hint: Soft, spongy ground that traps the walker.

poem_stanzas:
I am a season and a sudden source at once
When warmth returns, the orchard wakes in white
I bubble from a hidden crack in the hillside
The first green shoot, the bird's returning call

I mean the coiling metal that snaps back tight
I mean the water where the thirsty cattle drink
I mean the morning of the year's long story
And the leap of hope after the frost lets go
ciphers.hint: The season of blossom, or a coiled metal that snaps back.

poem_stanzas:
A wide mouth opened in the patient stone
So deep the river at the bottom is a whisper
Birds cross my emptiness and never look down
And echoes fall for ages before they land

Bridges tiptoe over me on trembling legs
I split the mountain into two cold halves
No rope can sound my bottom, no shout return
I am the earth's long wound that will not close
ciphers.hint: A deep, gaping cleft in the land.

poem_stanzas:
A silken sleeping bag spun from my own body
I hang in a tree like a small brown lantern
Inside me a soft creature turns to soup and dreams
Then wakes with wings it never had before

No door, no window, just a patient weave
I am the cradle and the coffin and the gate
When I split open, the air is suddenly a stranger
And something beautiful stumbles into the light
ciphers.hint: The silk house where a caterpillar transforms.

poem_stanzas:
A humming city with no streets but honeycomb
Ten thousand sisters working in the dark
I hang from a branch or sit on a wooden shelf
And guard a golden treasury of wax

One queen sleeps at my heart while workers toil
My citizens dance directions to the flowers
Disturb me and I answer with a sting
And sweet amber drips from every cell
ciphers.hint: The buzzing home of a colony of bees.

poem_stanzas:
A tunnel dug by small persistent hands
A dark warm room beneath the farmer's field
I have no rent and no address and no lamp
Just roots that dangle through my earthen roof

Rabbits, moles, and foxes know me well
I keep my tenants safe from hawk and frost
I am a doorway with no door at all
A secret street beneath the meadow's skin
ciphers.hint: An underground home dug by a rabbit.

poem_stanzas:
A cradle of twigs and grass and stolen fluff
Built in the fork of a tree or under the eaves
I hold small speckled treasures, warm and still
While a parent circles, scolding, overhead

I am made anew each year and then abandoned
A cup of patience woven without hands
When autumn strips the branches, I am found
An empty bowl that once held the sky
ciphers.hint: A bird's woven home for its eggs.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny star that leaps from flint or wire
The first bright thought before the fire begins
I live for one blue instant and then I pass
But I have started every flame that ever burned

Rub two things together and I appear
I jump the gap that should have kept me still
I am the messenger of lightning and of engines
The smallest seed of the oldest fire
ciphers.hint: A tiny flash that starts a fire.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow throat of water between two lands
So tight that ships must pass in single file
I join two seas that long to be one again
And separate two shores that almost touch

Named for the danger of my churning tides
I am the doorway of a continent
No river, no lake, but a corridor of salt
Where the ocean hurries through a slender gate
ciphers.hint: A narrow channel joining two seas.

poem_stanzas:
A water road between two banks of earth
Cut by nature or by careful hands
I carry boats where the land would rather stand
A path that flows instead of one that's walked

On your television I mean a different thing
A wavelength where a picture finds its home
But in the world of maps I am a bed of water
Guiding the tide between two quiet shores
ciphers.hint: The bed along which a river or sea flows.

poem_stanzas:
Where ships come home with salt upon their hulls
A harbor town with cranes and rusty chains
I am a doorway on the edge of the sea
Where journeys end and other journeys wait

On a computer I am a numbered gate
In wine I am a sweet fortified drink
But on a coast I am the haven and the dock
The place where the land shakes hands with the tide
ciphers.hint: A town where ships load and unload.

poem_stanzas:
Dark as a moonless night and slow as sleep
I pour like liquid time from a tilted tin
I am the thick blood left after the cane is crushed
And the poor man's sugar in a hungry year

Gingerbread and rum remember me
I am sweet but bitter, heavy but beloved
Ants will march for miles to find my trail
And winter puddings wait for my dark ribbon
ciphers.hint: Thick dark syrup left after refining sugar.

poem_stanzas:
A wobbly ending to a proper meal
I can be steamed, or chilled, or set in a mold
The British boil me in a cloth for hours
And call me Christmas when the raisins swell

I am not a cake and not a custard quite
I tremble when the spoon comes near my side
You may find me chocolate, rice, or sticky toffee
But always I am the sweet that follows dinner
ciphers.hint: A sweet dish served after the main course.

poem_stanzas:
A warm bowl of oats stirred in a pot
Breakfast for a bear and for a chilly child
I steam on winter mornings in a humble kitchen
And stick to the ribs till noon comes round

Goldilocks found me too hot and then too cold
Then just right, and ate me to the last spoon
I am simple, cheap, and filling to the core
The oldest start to a working day
ciphers.hint: A hot breakfast of oats boiled in milk or water.

poem_stanzas:
Born in a long green pod on a climbing vine
I am the second-most precious spice by weight
My tiny dark seeds fleck a scoop of ice cream
And perfume the air of every bakery

Synthetic versions sit in cheap bottles
But the real me comes from a patient orchid
I am sweet, warm, and utterly familiar
The quiet ghost in cake and custard both
ciphers.hint: The fragrant flavouring taken from an orchid pod.

poem_stanzas:
I wobble on a plate in bright red squares
Held together by nothing you can see
Children love me at a birthday feast
And I shiver when the spoon comes down

Fruit juice and sugar, set by a magic powder
I am not jam, though we are cousins still
I quiver like a coward in the bowl
And melt to syrup if you leave me warm
ciphers.hint: A wobbly fruit dessert set with gelatine.

poem_stanzas:
Bitter and golden, scraped from the peel
A breakfast spread the Scots hold dear
I am not jam, for I am tart not sweet
And bits of rind still float inside my glass

Oranges and sugar boiled into a jewel
Paddington's favourite on a slice of toast
I come in jars with gingham on the lid
And stain your fingers sticky in the morning
ciphers.hint: A tart citrus spread for toast.

poem_stanzas:
Sour as a lemon's grudge, I bite the tongue
I am wine that went too far and turned to sharpness
I pickle onions and I clean the glass
And make the fish and chips taste right

Four thieves once bathed in me to cheat the plague
I am the acid heart of salad dressing
Chips cry for me and sailors kept me close
I am the tang that wakes a sleepy meal
ciphers.hint: A sour liquid used in dressing and pickling.

poem_stanzas:
Bright and bruising, I come in a little jar
I bite the back of the nose and make eyes water
Yellow as a sun or grainy as a stone
I sit beside the sausage and the beef

A seed ground small, mixed with water and wine
I was once a tiny grain in a field of gold
The French and the English argue over my heat
But I am the sharp companion of the plate
ciphers.hint: A hot yellow condiment made from seeds.

poem_stanzas:
Red as a postbox, thick and slow to pour
I am the tomato's most famous disguise
I live in a bottle that needs a good hard shake
And children drown their chips and eggs in me

Sugar, salt, and vinegar hide the vegetable
I was once a Chinese fish sauce, strange but true
Now I am the darling of the dinner table
And the last thing left upon the plate
ciphers.hint: A sweet red sauce made from tomatoes.

poem_stanzas:
Pale and creamy, born of eggs and oil
I am an emulsion, a scientific trick
I crown the salad and I coat the chips
And turn a plain sandwich into a feast

Whisk me slowly or I will split and fail
The French claim me, the Dutch take my name
I am the cool white blanket on the bread
And the quiet base of a thousand sauces
ciphers.hint: A thick creamy dressing of egg and oil.

poem_stanzas:
Thick and white, I live in a little tub
Soured on purpose by tiny living friends
I come from milk that learned to keep
Long before the fridge was ever dreamed

Greeks strain me until I stand like cream
I wear fruit at the bottom or honey on top
Spoon me cold at breakfast or in curry
A cultured thing, and proud of it
ciphers.hint: A tangy set milk eaten with a spoon.

poem_stanzas:
I rise to the top when the milk is left to rest
The richest part, the first to be skimmed away
Whip me with air and I stand in soft white peaks
On strawberries and scones I am the crown

I make the soup luxurious, the coffee mild
A cat may lap me, a cake may crave me
I am the opposite of skimmed and thin
The fat of the milk and the joy of the tea
ciphers.hint: The rich top layer of milk.

poem_stanzas:
A soft grey snow that falls from a paper bag
Ground from golden fields and sifted fine
I wear an apron's dust on every baker's hands
And without me the loaf is only stone

I thicken sauces and I blanket fish
I am the quiet beginning of the bread
White or wholemeal, self-raising or plain
The mill's fine powder, the kitchen's faithful friend
ciphers.hint: Ground grain used for baking.

poem_stanzas:
A sleeping speck that wakes in warm sweet water
I breathe out bubbles that lift the heavy dough
Brewers and bakers both depend on me
A living thing too small to ever see

Give me sugar and I will multiply
Deny me warmth and I will sulk and die
I am the unseen hand that makes bread rise
The patient engine of the loaf
ciphers.hint: A living raising agent that makes bread rise.

poem_stanzas:
A lump of clay you must not bake until it rests
Flour and water wedded into something soft
I wait beneath a cloth to double in size
Kneaded by knuckles till I turn elastic

Pizza, bread, and biscuits all begin as me
Raw and pale, I am no one's dinner yet
I am the shapeless promise of the oven
A sticky ball of possibility
ciphers.hint: The soft uncooked mixture used to make bread.

poem_stanzas:
Flour, fat, and ice-cold water crumbled fine
Rolled into sheets as thin as a winter breath
I cradle the pie and I wall the tart
And shatter into flakes at the touch of a fork

Puff me by folding butter again and again
Short me and I crumble, sweeten me for dessert
A baker's hands must keep me cool and quick
Or I will turn to leather in the heat
ciphers.hint: Baked dough wrapped around a pie filling.

poem_stanzas:
A little pillow dropped into boiling broth
Flour and suet, or a pocket full of meat
I bob to the surface when I am finally done
And warm the belly on a freezing night

In China I am pleated in a bamboo basket
In England I sit atop a stew
Round and humble, I hide my treasure inside
A soft surprise that floats in the pot
ciphers.hint: A small ball of dough cooked in liquid or steamed.

poem_stanzas:
A slow conversation of meat and root
Left to murmur for hours on a low flame
I am thicker than soup and kinder than hunger
The peasant's feast and the winter's cure

Carrots, onions, and barley sink and soften
The house grows rich with the smell of my patience
Serve me in a bowl with bread to mop
I am time itself, made warm and edible
ciphers.hint: A slow-cooked dish of meat and vegetables.

poem_stanzas:
A covered dish that goes from oven to table
Layers of meat and vegetable baked as one
My name is both the food and the pot that holds it
A midweek meal from a busy mother's hand

Green beans and mushroom soup hide inside me
I bubble under a crust of cheese or crumb
No fuss, no flame, just patient steady heat
And leftovers that taste better the next day
ciphers.hint: A one-dish oven-baked meal, and the pot it cooks in.

poem_stanzas:
The inner bark of a tree rolled into a quill
Sweet and warm, I scent the winter kitchen
I dust the cappuccino and the morning bun
And hide in apple pie and mulled red wine

Once worth more than silver, sought across the sea
I am a spice that smells of hearth and home
Break me and I perfume the whole room
The curled brown stick of comfort and of heat
ciphers.hint: A sweet warming spice from rolled tree bark.

poem_stanzas:
A soft white cloud that waits upon the bed
I hold your head when the long day is done
Feathers or foam, I am stuffed with dreams
And flattened by the weight of eight hours

In a fight I fly across the room
Aircraft carry me for sleepy travellers
I am the quiet partner of the night
And the first thing you punch when morning comes
ciphers.hint: A soft cushion for resting your head at night.

poem_stanzas:
A hanging cloth that keeps the daylight out
I stand at the window like a folded skirt
Draw me and the room becomes a cave
The world may knock but I decide who sees

Velvet, lace, or plain, I divide the stage
I fall at the end of every play
In a shower I am a plastic sheet
And over a window I am the evening's gate
ciphers.hint: Cloth hung to cover a window or a stage.

poem_stanzas:
A tall white tower with a lamp for a heart
I sweep a bright arm across the black water
Sailors far from shore trust my steady blink
And steer their hulls away from the hungry rocks

I stand where the land ends and the sea begins
Wind and salt have weathered my stone for years
I ask for nothing and I sleep by day
But when night falls I am the coast's one eye
ciphers.hint: A tower that warns ships with a flashing light.

poem_stanzas:
A giant with four arms that never tires
The breeze turns me and I grind the grain to dust
Don Quixote charged me with a lance
And in Holland I once pumped the sea away

I am the old machine that drank the breeze
Before the turbine stole my place and name
My sails go round and round above the fields
A gentle giant of the flat green land
ciphers.hint: A building whose sails spin to grind grain or pump water.

poem_stanzas:
A thousand small pieces scattered on the floor
Only when I am whole do you see the scene
I tease the mind and beg for patient hands
And the last piece is always the hardest to find

A riddle, a maze, or a jigsaw on the table
I am the pleasure of a problem solved
Crossword, jigsaw, or a tangled knot
I hide my picture in plain scattered sight
ciphers.hint: A game or picture broken into pieces to solve.

poem_stanzas:
A round hollow that cups the morning cereal
I hold the soup and warm the cupped hands
In a stadium I am the great game itself
And on the table I am the humble curve

I am not a plate, for I have walls and depth
Wooden, china, or a golden fish
I cradle the batter and I mix the cake
And the last drop of porridge scrapes my side
ciphers.hint: A round deep dish for soup or cereal.

poem_stanzas:
I am a small round vessel with a handle on my side
I hold the tea, the coffee, and the cheer
In sport I am a trophy raised in triumph
And a measure in every recipe you read

Fill me too full and I will spill my heat
I wear the ring of a thousand sips
I am comfort held in two warm palms
The morning's first companion and its last
ciphers.hint: A small drinking vessel with a handle.

poem_stanzas:
A shallow little plate that waits beneath a drink
I catch the drips and keep the table dry
Little dishes of milk were set out for the cat
And flying ones bring visitors from the stars

I am the smaller circle under the larger one
Plain or painted with a rose and vine
I am the quiet shadow and the throne
A disc of porcelain, waiting to be used
ciphers.hint: A small shallow dish placed under a cup.

poem_stanzas:
A round-bellied vessel with a spout and a lid
I sing when the water inside me boils
I pour the comfort of a hundred cups
And my whistle calls the family to the table

I am short and stout, and tipped to pour
My handle is my ear, my spout my nose
I steep the leaves until the water turns gold
And a cosy keeps me warm when the fire dies
ciphers.hint: A pot with a spout for brewing and pouring tea.

poem_stanzas:
A little plug that keeps the bottle's secret
Cork or glass, I seal the narrow neck
Pull me out and the wine at last can breathe
Push me in and the fizz must stay and wait

I fill the hole and hold the liquid in
Rubber in a sink, a cork in the neck
Without me the contents trickle out and spoil
The small guardian of every opened jar
ciphers.hint: A plug that seals the neck of a bottle.

poem_stanzas:
A metal heart with a keyhole for a mouth
I keep the door and guard the hidden room
Turn me and the bolt slides home with a click
Without the right shape I will not give way

On a canal I am the water's step and gate
In your hair I am a tangled curl
I am the small cold guardian of your things
And a puzzle of brass that only one key solves
ciphers.hint: A fastening opened with a key.

poem_stanzas:
A metal joint that lets the door swing free
I creak and groan for want of a little oil
Without me the panel would only slide or stand
I am the elbow of the swinging gate

Two plates and a pin, bolted fast to wood
I turn a cupboard's face into a moving wall
Hushed into silence by a single drop of oil
And every opening doorway owes me thanks
ciphers.hint: A joint on which a door or lid swings.

poem_stanzas:
A brass or porcelain ball you turn to enter
Cold in the winter, warm from many hands
I sit at the middle of every arrival
And decide whether you may come inside

A house can stand without me but is poor
I am the round full stop at the end of the hall
Wild and loose I rattle and refuse
And polished bright by years of daily grip
ciphers.hint: The round handle you turn to open a door.

poem_stanzas:
A bar or knobby grip fixed to a thing
I let your hand command the heavy door
On a cup you call me by another name
And beside a name I am what people call you

Pull me, push me, turn me, lift me too
I am affixed to pan, to chest, to blade
Without me the tool is clumsy and bites
The place your fingers know before your eyes
ciphers.hint: The part you grip to open, carry, or use something.

poem_stanzas:
A circle that turns and carries the cart
The oldest invention of the rolling world
Rim, spoke, and hub, I sing upon the road
And without me your journey would only drag

In a car I am four, on a bike I am two
In a fortune I turn with the fates of men
In a pot I am round and ready to bake
I am the shape of motion itself, rolling on
ciphers.hint: A round part that turns to move a vehicle.

poem_stanzas:
I bite a hole through wood and steel and wall
A spinning spiral with a hungry point
The dentist owns a small and screaming kind
And the soldier learns to march on my command

Squeeze my trigger and I whine and bore
I come in a box with many sizes of bit
I make the way for screws and nails to follow
The piercing tool that opens what was closed
ciphers.hint: A tool that spins to bore a hole.

poem_stanzas:
A thin blade with a row of little teeth
I eat through timber with a grinding song
Carpenters push and pull me to and fro
And I split the log into a plank

I have a handle and a toothy edge
I bite the branch that the gardener wants gone
My name is also a thing your eyes have done
And an old saying about what the eyes have done
ciphers.hint: A toothed tool for cutting wood.

poem_stanzas:
A sticky white river that hardens into rock
I mend the broken cup and the torn page
Squeeze me from a bottle or melt me in a pot
And two things part no more when I have dried

I hold the model plane and the broken chair
I smell of school and paper and desperate hands
I am the quiet promise that things can be fixed
And the reason your fingers are stuck together
ciphers.hint: A sticky substance for joining things together.

poem_stanzas:
A long thin ribbon wound around a wheel
I stick and seal and patch and bind
Transparent or brown, I mend the torn box
And measure you against a wall of marks

I come in rolls for wrapping and for mending
In a recorder I hold a voice from long ago
At the finish line I am the chest that wins
A sticky strip that holds the world together
ciphers.hint: A sticky strip used to stick or record things.

poem_stanzas:
A thin twisted cord that ties and binds
On a puppet I make the little man dance
On a violin I sing beneath a bow
And in a code I am a line of symbols

I can be a shoelace or a kite's long tail
I come on a ball for cats to chase
I hold the parcel and I pull the blind
A slender cord that serves a thousand uses
ciphers.hint: A thin cord used to tie or bind.

poem_stanzas:
A fine spun line that runs through the eye of a needle
I am the thin lifeline of every cloth
Follow me through the maze and you will escape
And cut me and the whole garment unravels

I come on a spool in many a colour
I sew the button and I darn the sock
In a story I am a recurring theme
And in the web I am every strand
ciphers.hint: A fine strand of spun fibre used in sewing.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny metal spike with a round head
I hold the cloth and I burst the balloon
On a map I mark the place you dream of
And on a badge I fasten it to your coat

I am a number you must remember for money
I hold the seam until the stitch is done
In bowling I am the skittle standing tall
And a needle's plain and headless cousin
ciphers.hint: A short thin piece of metal with a sharp point.

poem_stanzas:
A row of interlocking teeth on a moving track
I close a jacket, a bag, a tent, a fly
One little slider brings my two halves together
And one quick tug can open me again

I am the sound of dressing in the morning
I guard your pocket and I seal your case
Metal or plastic, I run up and down
The neatest way to shut a gap of cloth
ciphers.hint: A fastening with interlocking teeth, pulled by a slider.

poem_stanzas:
A strip of leather that circles the waist
I keep your trousers where they ought to be
In a machine I carry power round a pulley
And in the sky I am a band of stars

I buckle and I loosen, I have holes and a tongue
I hold the tools of a working man
In karate I mark how far you have come
And a good hard pull can drive a fan
ciphers.hint: A strap worn around the waist.

poem_stanzas:
A strong band that holds and lifts and binds
On a bag I ride upon the shoulder
On a watch I circle the narrow wrist
And in a bus I am the bar you clutch

I keep the case shut and the horse in line
I am the thing you pull to tighten load
Leather or nylon, I bear the weight for you
A faithful band that never lets things fall
ciphers.hint: A strip of material used to fasten or carry.

poem_stanzas:
A tough white band that ties bone to bone
I hold the joint together when you run
Twist too far and I will tear and burn
The surgeon's needle mends me if I break

I am not the cord that pulls the limb
But the quiet tether of the skeleton
Without me the knee would wander loose and wild
I am the strong, silent binding of the frame
ciphers.hint: Tough tissue that connects bone to bone.

poem_stanzas:
The flat side of the head above the cheek
Where the pulse beats faintly near the hair
An ancient house of worship shares my name
And a place of honour in Japan as well

I frame the eye and hold the brow aloft
Grey with worry, or kissed by a mother
I am the smooth wall at the side of the skull
And a grand building with a columned face
ciphers.hint: The flat part of the head beside the eye.

poem_stanzas:
The round back of the foot below the ankle
I strike the ground first when you stride
Achilles met his end beside my cord
And a hard crust at the end of the loaf

In wrestling I am the villain's move
On a shoe I am stacked and raised
I grind the soil when you dig in and push
The patient base that lifts the whole frame
ciphers.hint: The back part of the foot below the ankle.

poem_stanzas:
A bony basket woven round the heart
Twelve pairs of curved and springy bars
I rise and fall with every breath you take
And shield the soft organs from any sudden blow

I am a cage that holds no captive bird
Cedar and bone both build me in their way
I arch above the liver and the gut
The body's coracle upon the tide of air
ciphers.hint: The bony frame that protects the chest organs.

poem_stanzas:
The hinged bone that lets you speak and chew
I carry the lower row of biting teeth
Samson slew a thousand with my like
And a donkey's weapon in an old story

I move when you yawn and when you shout
The dentist takes my picture with a beam
I am the cradle of the chin below
And the door of the mouth that swings all day
ciphers.hint: The bone that forms the lower jaw.

poem_stanzas:
The ridge beneath the eye that catches light
I give the face its proud and hollow glance
A fist can bruise me purple in a fight
And models praise the high and sculpted line

I arch across from ear to nose
I frame the smile and hold the flesh in place
The bone the blush comes rising over
The feature that makes a face a face
ciphers.hint: The bone forming the prominence below the eye.

poem_stanzas:
A small hard shield upon the fingertip
I grow from the root and never stop
I protect the tender pad below me
And I am painted red for a party

I can be bitten, filed, or trimmed
I leave a scratch upon the careless skin
The white half-moon sits at my base
And I am the armour at the end of the hand
ciphers.hint: The hard plate covering the tip of a finger.

poem_stanzas:
A broad flat tooth far back in the jaw
I grind the food the front teeth only tear
I have my own set of deep and stubborn roots
And the dentist fills me when I ache

I am not the sharp one and not the chisel one
I am the millstone of the mouth
A name I share with a measure in chemistry
And the last to erupt, the wisdom kind
ciphers.hint: A large grinding tooth at the back of the mouth.

poem_stanzas:
The soft back of the neck beneath the hair
Where a mother's hand rests and a lover's breath
A vampire's favourite and a barber's care
And the place a warm shiver likes to start

I am the gentle hollow under the skull
Where the collar rests and the ponytail swings
The tender slope between shoulder and head
The vulnerable curve that asks to be stroked
ciphers.hint: The back of the neck.

poem_stanzas:
The broad hinge where the arm meets the trunk
I carry bags, burdens, and the world
Tap me and you give a lucky sign
Or offer me to one who weeps

I am rounded, and I am a road's edge
I bear the yoke and the heavy pack
I slump when you are tired or ashamed
And I shrug when you truly do not care
ciphers.hint: The joint where the arm joins the body.

poem_stanzas:
The scaffolding of bone beneath the skin
Two hundred pieces in a silent frame
I grin at you from every cupboard door
And clatter when the warrior is stripped

I hold the body upright like a tent's poles
Miners find me in the ancient rock
I have a key to almost every form
And a closet full of family secrets
ciphers.hint: The bony framework that supports the body.

poem_stanzas:
A giant of the northern forest and the marsh
My antlers crown the tallest of my kind
I bugle in the autumn for a mate
And browse the willow in the cold grey dawn

I am a cousin of the deer and the moose
Larger than a stag, with a shaggy mane
In Europe they call me by a different name
And a famous club takes me for its badge
ciphers.hint: A large deer of northern forests.

poem_stanzas:
A hunter of the African night
My laugh rings over the carcass and the plain
My shoulders stand taller than my sloping back
And my jaws crush the bone the lion leaves

I am called a coward though I hunt in packs
I whoop and giggle in the dark
An old cartoon made me a grinning fool
But my bite is the strongest for my size
ciphers.hint: A laughing scavenger of African plains.

poem_stanzas:
A small and sturdy cousin of the horse
I carry children round the paddock ring
My tail is docked and my mane is thick
And my name is a coin in British slang

I am not a foal, though I stand so low
Shetland, Exmoor, and the Welsh hills know me
I trot all day and never seem to tire
And I give small riders their first taste of speed
ciphers.hint: A small breed of horse.

poem_stanzas:
A woolly baby of the springtime field
I skip beside my mother in the green
The butcher's word for my tender meat
And the quiet symbol of the innocent

I bleat a small and wobbling cry
Mary's little follower, white as milk
I am shorn each year for the fleece I grow
And a lion and I shall lie down together
ciphers.hint: A young sheep.

poem_stanzas:
I crow the sun up from behind the hill
My comb is red, my wattle hangs below
I strut the yard like a feathered king
And I wake the farmer long before the alarm

I am a male of the barnyard flock
A weathervane is shaped in my likeness
I guard the hens and ruffle at a rival
And my voice is the sound of a country dawn
ciphers.hint: The crowing male of the henhouse.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny brown bird with a cocked-up tail
I sing with a voice too big for my size
I nest in a hedge or a garden pot
And I am the king of all the birds, they say

I flit through the brambles, secretive and quick
The smallest of the common garden kinds
I raise a brood in a mossy dome
And a great cathedral dome honours my name
ciphers.hint: A tiny brown garden bird with a cocked tail.

poem_stanzas:
A fork-tailed bird that skims the summer air
I fly from Africa and back each year
I build a cup of mud beneath the eaves
And I signal that the warm days have returned

I cannot truly eat while standing still
I drink upon the wing and catch my prey
One act of mine means to take a thing in
A proverb warns one does not make a summer
ciphers.hint: A fork-tailed migrant bird, or to take in food.

poem_stanzas:
A white bird of the harbor and the pier
My cry is the sound of a seaside town
I steal your chips and wheel above the ferry
And I follow the trawler for its scraps

I am grey on the back and white below
My feet are webbed and orange as my beak
I circle the cliff where my colony nests
And I ride the wind without a single flap
ciphers.hint: A common white coastal bird.

poem_stanzas:
A fire that climbs the throat and roars
I turn the fist to stone and the voice to thunder
I am the red you see before the blow
And the shame that follows when the storm has passed

I am the opposite of calm and cool
A bull may see me in a waving cloth
I fill the room and drive the wise to folly
And I am the fever that makes the strong go blind
ciphers.hint: Violent, uncontrollable anger.

poem_stanzas:
A sudden stampede of the frightened mind
I seize the breath and send the heart to gallop
Named for a goat-legged god of old
I turn a crowd into a crushing wave

I am the alarm that comes before the danger
I scatter the sensible and scatter the wise
My brother is calm, who arrives too late
I am the scream inside before the sound
ciphers.hint: Sudden overwhelming fear that spreads through a crowd.

poem_stanzas:
A sweet and aching look at days long gone
I am a homesickness for a time, not a place
I smell of an old house and a summer evening
And I turn the past to gold we never had

The Greek words for a homecoming and its pain
I live in old photographs and grandparents' songs
I soften memory until it glows
And I make the grown heart long to be small
ciphers.hint: A wistful longing for the past.

poem_stanzas:
The cool breath after the fever breaks
I am the loosening of a knot in the chest
I arrive when the feared thing does not come
And I am the sigh that ends a long-held worry

I am a carving on a temple wall
I am the letting-go of a heavy weight
I follow the news that all is well at last
And I am the opposite of dread and strain
ciphers.hint: The easing of worry or pain.

poem_stanzas:
A breath shaped into the faintest word
I am a secret passed beside an ear
I live where a crowd must not hear
And leaves and lovers both have used my voice

I am softer than speech and louder than thought
I travel the length of a library unbroken
In a storm I am the wind among the pines
And a ghost would speak to you in me
ciphers.hint: To speak very softly and quietly.

poem_stanzas:
A room with no sound but its own weight
I am what follows the last note fades
I am golden, they say, and deeper than speech
And I can be a comfort or a threat

I am kept, I am broken, I am heavy, I am awkward
In a sacred place I am the shape of awe
A pause between two claps holds me complete
And the loudest of all is the moment I end
ciphers.hint: Complete absence of sound.

poem_stanzas:
I tell you not where you go but how fast
I am speed with a direction firmly fixed
An arrow's flight, a rocket's climb, a fall
And a physicist's arrow upon a graph

I am measured in metres for every second
Change me and you change the thing called force
I am the vector, the rate of a moving place
And the police may stop you for my excess
ciphers.hint: The speed of something in a given direction.

poem_stanzas:
The push a moving thing will not give up
I am mass in motion, stubborn and heavy
I carry the train long past the brake
And I am what a collision cannot ignore

I am born of speed and bulk together
A rolling stone gathers me as it goes
Once I am begun I hate to turn
And a crowd can gather me as it grows
ciphers.hint: The force of a moving object; impetus gained by movement.

poem_stanzas:
A box of quiet lightning kept for later
I hold two poles that long to meet
In a torch I light, in a phone I speak
And when my charge runs out the world goes dark

I have a positive and a negative end
I turn a sleeping current into a running one
A line of guns shares my name in battle
And I am a farm's long row of laying hens
ciphers.hint: A device that stores and supplies electric power.

poem_stanzas:
How often a thing repeats in a given time
I count the hum of the mains and the beat of a heart
Raise me and the note climbs higher and higher
And a radio searches me by the turn of a dial

I am the wedge between one wave and the next
I measure the passing of pulses and cycles
Invisible, yet a hertz is my little crown
And my opposite is the gap between two
ciphers.hint: The rate at which something repeats.

poem_stanzas:
A long great work for a hall of many players
Four movements in a single grand design
I am not the little tune a whistler knows
But the whole orchestra in ordered storm

Beethoven wrote nine, and a tenth he never made
My name is Greek for a sounding together
A conductor lifts his arms and I begin
And I am the largest form a player serves
ciphers.hint: A long orchestral work, usually in several movements.

poem_stanzas:
The speed at which the dancers take the floor
I hurry the quick and slow the solemn down
Musicians keep me with a tapping foot
And I am often measured in beats each minute

Italian words for fast and slow are mine
I can be a march, a gallop, or a crawl
I set the pulse the whole orchestra obeys
And I am the pace of any piece of music
ciphers.hint: The speed or pace of a piece of music.

poem_stanzas:
Eight steps of a scale from low to high
In me the same note comes around again
A woman and a man can sing the same one
And my name begins with the Latin for eight

I am the span from do to the do above
Piano keys repeat my pattern in a row
A choir finds me when the voices part
And I double or I halve a pitch
ciphers.hint: The interval of eight notes spanning a scale.

poem_stanzas:
A small dark mark upon a ladder of lines
I tell the voice how high and long to sing
I am also a short written word you leave
And the paper money in a Russian's wallet

I hold the time and the pitch in my little head
A scale is only me repeated eight times
On a door I tell you where to leave a message
And a singer strikes me high and strong
ciphers.hint: A single sound of a given pitch; also a short written message.

poem_stanzas:
A melody you whistle on the way to work
I am a sequence of sounds the ear can hold
I get stuck in your head and will not leave
And a piano is not in me until it is fixed

I am what a fiddler plays by ear
You hum me, you carry me, you tap me out
I can be sweet, or flat, or out of sorts
And they say a good one is hard to find
ciphers.hint: A melody, especially a memorable one.

poem_stanzas:
A half man, half fish of the deep blue sea
My tail splits where a person's legs would be
I comb my hair upon a lonely rock
And sailors claim to hear me sing at dusk

My sister is more famous than I am
My father holds a trident in the deep
I am the ocean's answer to a centaur
And I guard a drowned kingdom under the waves
ciphers.hint: A mythical male creature, half man and half fish.

poem_stanzas:
A bearded fellow with a pointed hat
I turn a prince to a frog and back again
I read the stars and mix a potent draught
And I command a staff to do my will

My cousin is a sorcerer or a mage
I live in a tower and I keep an owl
I duel with fireballs and vanish in a puff
And a certain school made me a famous name
ciphers.hint: A man with magical powers, often in folklore.

poem_stanzas:
A crone upon a broom across the moon
I stir a cauldron and I curse a cow
I wear a pointed hat and keep a black cat
And in Salem they burned my kind for sport

I am the wicked one who bakes a child
Or the good one who mends with herbs and charm
On Halloween I knock upon your door
And I melt when a bucket of water finds me
ciphers.hint: A woman believed to practise magic.

poem_stanzas:
Moving through water by your own strength
Four strokes compete to be the fastest kind
The frog and the crawl and the butterfly and back
And the one most learn first is the gentle dog

A pool is my arena and the lane is mine
You hold your breath and stroke and turn and glide
I am a sport and also the act of not drowning
And the sea and the bath both let me happen
ciphers.hint: Moving through water using the limbs.

poem_stanzas:
I travel by the grace of the wind alone
The boom, the sheet, the tack, the jibe are mine
I race the yachts around the buoyed course
And I need no fuel but the moving air

I set the canvas and I lean with the gust
The tiller and the rudder answer me
I am both a sport and a way to cross the ocean
And a landlocked man takes lessons just to learn me
ciphers.hint: Travelling on water using the power of the wind.

poem_stanzas:
I rise by hand and foot up a sheer face
Rope and carabiner are my trusted friends
I conquer the peak or I retreat in rain
And a mountain and a ladder both invite me

I am a sport of chalk and grip and nerve
Free, or aided, or upon an indoor wall
I am also what the vine does up the trellis
And the slow ascent of one who seeks the top
ciphers.hint: Ascending a rock face or mountain using hands and feet.
